title: Latency telemetry surface mapping and dashboard anti-patterns
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operator-focused note to map the end-to-end latency telemetry surface for tokenized inference paths and call out common dashboard anti-patterns we keep seeing in runbooks. Goal is to give a pragmatic checklist for engineers building dashboards and for oncall to quickly decide where to look when customers report perceived slowness.

High‑level model of request path (for telemetry mapping):
- API gateway / ingress: HTTP request arrival and auth overhead
- Routing & policy layer: tenant routing, rate-limit checks, route decision logic
- Queueing / scheduling: request enqueue, worker assignment, preflight checks
- Session & KV cache lookup: prefix cache, KV cache hits/misses, warm-starts
- Model dispatch: batching, bundle selection, model variant routing
- GPU/CPU inference: forward pass, softmax/decoder, quantization fallback
- Post-processing: response formatting, tooling-level function calls, streaming flush
- Egress: network write, client ack/close

Telemetry surfaces to capture (metric + suggested aggregation):
1) request_latency_ms (p50/p90/p99) - whole request from ingress->egress (tag by route, model, tenant, region)
2) ingress_parse_ms - time to parse/auth/validate request
3) routing_decision_ms - time spent in routing/policy evaluation (important for tenant tiering)
4) queue_time_ms - time in pre-scheduling queue (histogram buckets, per-worker-pool)
5) batching_delay_ms - delay introduced waiting for batch formation (per-model, per-sequence-length-bin)
6) kv_cache_hit_rate (percentage) - key per-tenant & model; broken into prefix_hit / full_kv_hit
7) kv_lookup_ms - median + tail when misses trigger model work
8) model_dispatch_ms - time to dispatch to model host + scheduling overhead
9) inference_compute_ms - GPU/CPU time (instrumented in-serving runtime) split by forward/backward/decoder steps if available
10) token_decode_ms_per_token - useful for long streaming responses
11) postprocess_ms - time spent in funneling output through safety/formatting/function-call steps
12) egress_write_ms - network write time and client ack stalls

Tracing guidance (span design & tags):
- One top-level span per request: tags: request_id, tenant_id, route, model, region, plan_tier
- Child spans for each telemetry surface above (ingress, routing, queue, kv-lookup, dispatch, inference, postprocess, egress)
- Include contextual metadata in spans: batch_size, sequence_length, kv_cache_status, fallback_variant (if any)
- For streaming responses, emit lightweight per-chunk spans or annotations rather than full child spans to avoid trace bloat
- Sampling: prioritize traces for p95/p99 requests and for any request that triggered a fallback (quantization fallback, cold_kv_miss, model_variant_fallback)
- Severity tagging: annotate spans with severity labels (latency-major, latency-minor, error) used by adaptive sampling policies

Sampling & retention heuristics (practical):
- Default low-rate sampling for steady-state (1-2%) to understand baseline flows
- Tail-focused burst sampling: for requests with request_latency_ms > p95 or that hit an error/fallback, up-sample to 100% for 10 minutes around the event window
- Tenant-aware sampling: high-revenue tenants get higher baseline sampling (e.g., 5-10%) but obey privacy/PII filters
- Trace retention tiers: brief hot retention (30d) for high-fidelity traces, aggregated span-metrics for 90–180d

Common dashboard anti-patterns and why they hurt investigations:
1) Single-panel request_latency_ms only (no decomposition)
   - Anti-pattern: Only shows global p95/p99.
   - Why bad: Masks root cause (queueing vs compute vs network). Forces noisy drilldowns.
2) Too many high-cardinality tags in single widgets
   - Anti-pattern: panels that attempt to break down by tenant, route, model, and instance simultaneously.
   - Why bad: Explodes query cost, slows dashboards, returns sparse/noisy data. Use pre-aggregated rollups or dropdown filters instead.
3) Per-instance heatmap without normalization
   - Anti-pattern: Showing raw latency per instance without request volume normalization.
   - Why bad: Low-volume instances show wild variance; ops chase non-actionable outliers.
4) Over-reliance on average metrics
   - Anti-pattern: Using mean/avg to judge performance.
   - Why bad: Tail latency matters for UX; prefer quantiles + throughput-aware visualization.
5) Full-trace replay panel that loads all spans for a time range
   - Anti-pattern: Auto-loading detailed traces for wide time windows.
   - Why bad: Query and retention blowup, slow UI. Only load traces on demand or sample a small set.
6) Mixing synthetic probe metrics and real user telemetry in the same SLI panel
   - Anti-pattern: One SLI graph that mixes canary probe latency with production p95.
   - Why bad: Corners cause misinterpretation; separate panels and label clearly.

Recommended dashboard composition (compact, investigation-first):
Top row - rapid triage:
- Global request_latency_ms (p50/p90/p99) with quick filters for region/model/route
- Traffic heatmap (requests/s) with per-tenant top movers
- Error rate (5xx, timeout) with link to recent trace samples

Second row - decomposition (side-by-side):
- Queue_time_ms p50/p95/p99 stacked with batching_delay_ms (shows scheduling vs batching tradeoffs)
- Inference_compute_ms (host-reported) vs kv_lookup_ms (to show cold misses impact)
- Batch_size distribution panel with correlation to latency quantiles

Third row - operational signals and knobs:
- KV cache warmth (percent of requests that are prefix-warm) + recent evictions spike
- Fallbacks and variant-switch counters (quantization_fallback, small_model_fallback)
- Worker pool saturation and scheduling backlog per-pool

Investigation checklist (quick ops play):
1) Confirm scope: single-tenant or system-wide? Check tenant filter + time window.
2) Compare request_latency and queue_time: if queue_time rises first, suspect scheduling pressure.
3) Check batch_size distribution: increase in tiny batches => upstream routing change or low request aggregation.
4) Look at kv_cache_hit_rate: cold_kv_miss spikes typically align with long tails (warm-start strategies needed).
5) Inspect traces for high-latency requests: identify which child span dominates (dispatch vs compute vs postprocess).
6) If fallback flags present in traces, follow variant fallback path: quantify % of affected requests.
7) Mitigation knobs: temporarily increase batch latency budget, add burst capacity, pin warm caches for critical tenants, or rollback recent routing/feature flag changes.

Practical instrumentation checklist for engineers (low-friction priorities):
- Emit request-level histogram for end-to-end latency with route/model/tenant tags.
- Ensure queue_time and inference_compute are emitted as separate metrics with same request_id for trace linking.
- Add boolean metric/annotation for kv_cache_status (hit/miss/partial) on request completions.
- Record batch_size and sequence_length as low-cardinality labels (e.g., small/medium/large bins) to avoid cardinality blowup.
- Add a "fallback_reason" tag when a request uses a non-default model variant or quantization fallback.

UI/Query cost guidance:
- Build pre-aggregated rollups for common slices (by route/model/tenant-day-hour) to support fast dashboards without heavy ad-hoc queries.
- Use histogram quantiles server-side where available to avoid expensive client-side quantile stitching.
- Cap widget time ranges for automatic refresh to 1h or 6h by default; allow manual extension for deep dives.

Open questions / followups: (for next telemetry grooming session)
- Do we want a lightweight per-tenant SLIs page that surfaces only critical signals for billing-tiered customers? (owner: product-observability)
- Should we standardize batch_size bins and implement a shared metrics lib for sequence_length bucketing? (owner: runtime-instrumentation)
- Proposal: add an adaptive trace-sampling rule for any request where queue_time_ms > X ms AND inference_compute_ms > Y ms so we capture weird multi-layer tails. (owner: eng-observability)

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Wire up a sample dashboard JSON for the top-row triage view and add to github telemetry-widgets repo (low priority).
- Schedule 60-minute workshop with runtime, routing, and SRE to converge on canonical metric names and label sets (target: Q1 2026).

End.
